name: Gilberto LERENA (Gilberto Justiniano LERENA LENGUAS)
occupation: CORREDOR DE COMERCIO (commercial broker), per the 1895 census; breeder and co-founder of the Argentine Stud Book
source: 1895 Argentine national census, Seccion 21; and baptism act No. 1447 of 31 Oct 1886, San Francisco de Asis - IMAGE READ; and baptism of his son Raul Alfredo Luis, Catedral Basilica de Montevideo, 10 Sep 1885 - IMAGE READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-BQZD-W
note: *** Co-founder of the Argentine Stud Book; a Group 1 at Palermo renamed for him in 1914. A Lerena at the centre of Argentine thoroughbred breeding, in the right country at the right time - and PABLO ARMANDO TRAINED AND OWNED RACEHORSES. *** Born Montevideo 24 May 1855, died 8 December 1912. His father is now documented rather than asserted: his brother Luis Eugenio's marriage act of 19 December 1864 names their parents as Don Luis and Dona Justiniana Lenguas. That he and Luis Eugenio are BROTHERS still rests on published genealogy, not on an act, and is marked secondary on the charts. *** NO PROVEN LINK TO PABLO ARMANDO. *** *** HIS PARENTS ARE NOW NAMED, 13 September 2026: LUIS LERENA and JUSTINIANA LENGUAS. *** Two independent Uruguayan parish records, entered for two different children of his, both give his parents so. That makes him A BROTHER OF LUIS EUGENIO LERENA LENGUAS - the same Montevideo household that produced the one Lerena baptism in Rosario before 1879. The racing dynasty and the Rosario thread are the same family. *** THE IMAGE IS NOW OPENED, AND IT IS PRIMARY. *** Act 1447 of 31 October 1886 baptises his daughter Maria Angelica Julia, "hija legitima de Don Gilberto Lerena y de Dona Julia Salvanach, orientales", and names the paternal grandparents "Don LUIS y Dona JUSTINIANA LENGUAS" - the same couple named as Luis Eugenio's parents in his marriage act of 1864 and his death act of 1901. *** AND THE GODMOTHER IS DONA JULIA JUANICO DE LERENA - Luis Eugenio's own wife, standing at the font for her husband's brother's daughter. *** The two households are one family acting as one. Written by Martin Perez, the same priest who wrote act 1720 for Candido Jaime that year. *** AND A SECOND ACT, FROM A DIFFERENT PARISH, SAYS THE SAME, 14 September 2026: *** the baptism of his son Raul Alfredo Luis at the Catedral Basilica on 10 September 1885 gives "abuelos paternos: Luis y Justiniana Lenguas" and "abuelos maternos: Cristobal y Angela Alvarez" - identical to act 1447, in a different year, a different parish and a different priest's hand. Its godmother is a JOSEFA LERENA otherwise unknown to this archive. *** HIS HOUSEHOLD IS NOW ASSEMBLED, 14 September 2026: EIGHT CHILDREN by Julia Salvanach *** - Gilberto (1878), Carlos (1884), Raul Alfredo Luis (1885), Maria Angelica Julia (1886), all born at Montevideo; then Maria Carlota (1890), Luis Felipe (1892), Cesar Alberto (1896) and Horacio Alfredo (1898), at Buenos Aires. *** THE LAST MONTEVIDEO BAPTISM IS 31 OCTOBER 1886 AND THE FIRST BUENOS AIRES ONE 29 OCTOBER 1890, which brackets the family's crossing between those dates *** - firmer than the "1887 to 1889" this archive read off census birthplaces. AND JUAN CARLOS IS NOT AMONG THEM. *** AND THE 1895 CENSUS SCHEDULE, READ AS A HOUSEHOLD FOR THE FIRST TIME ON 14 September 2026, GIVES HIM A TRADE: CORREDOR DE COMERCIO - a commercial broker, aged 41, casado, R. Oriental, catolico. *** This archive has had him as a breeder, which is what he is remembered for; in his own house he told the enumerator he was a broker.

name: Maria Julia Margarita Josefa Emirena Justiniana LERENA Juanico (m. HERRERA)
source: Rosario baptism, Libro 15 folio 229, act 1541, bapt. 17 Feb 1866; Montevideo marriage, San Francisco de Asis, act 1879, 3 Nov 1886; and La Union religious marriage register act 90, 30 June 1913 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-T7P2-W
note: *** The only LERENA baptised at Rosario between 1731 and 1901 - and now followed to the end of the story. *** Born 8 October 1865, baptised at Rosario 17 February 1866 to Don Luis Lerena Lenguas and Dona Julia Juanico, "naturales del E. Oriental". On 3 November 1886, aged 21, she married Don Jaime Herrera at San Francisco de Asis, Ciudad Vieja, MONTEVIDEO - the act naming her parents again, in a second country, twenty years later. She went home. *** NOT the Maria Lerena who was Pablo Armando's mother: that woman had a son in February 1882, when this one was sixteen and four years from marrying someone else. *** *** HER SURNAME IS CORRECTED HERE, 14 September 2026, and an act says so. *** This register called her *** LERENA LENGUAS *** - which is her FATHER'S compound, not hers. Her father was Luis Lerena Lenguas; her mother was Julia Juanico; *** so she is LERENA JUANICO, exactly as her siblings Ema Sixta and Candido Jaime are already named on their own rows here. *** She was the odd one out and nothing had caught it. *** THE EVIDENCE IS THE ACT READ TODAY: *** at her sister Ema Sixta's wedding on 30 June 1913 the witnesses are written *** "Don Jaime Herrera y Dona Maria Perena Juanico de Herrera" *** - her own compound, in her own lifetime, with PERENA the machine's usual mangling of LERENA on this family. *** IT ALSO MATTERED FOR THE CHECKING: *** the compound-surname sibling test keys on the two surnames in a row's name, so while she read LERENA LENGUAS she was being grouped with her father's generation instead of with her own brothers and sisters.

name: Don Luis Eugenio LERENA LENGUAS
source: Montevideo civil death registration No. 216, 24 December 1901 - IMAGE READ; plus Rosario baptism act 1541 (1866) and Montevideo marriage act 258 (1864); and his own baptism, La Mauricia, Villa de la Union, 7 Jan 1846 - IMAGE READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-ZS62-J; and the Montevideo Direccion de Cementerios mortality return for December 1901 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3QHK-XQ11-BC6G
note: *** DOCUMENTED, 13 September 2026. *** "Natural de esta Republica", married Dona Julia Juanico at San Francisco de Asis, Ciudad Vieja, Montevideo, on 19 December 1864 - act 258, image read - which names him "hijo legitimo de Don Luis y de Dona Justiniana Lenguas". His daughter Laura Adela's baptism of 1869 names the same two as her paternal grandparents, independently. So his parentage is PRIMARY, not the tree assertion it was that morning; and it makes him a brother of GILBERTO JUSTINIANO LERENA LENGUAS, co-founder of the Argentine Stud Book - though THAT brotherhood still rests on published genealogy rather than an act, and is marked secondary on the chart. Five children, all on primary records. Died before 11 July 1910, when his widow's death was registered. *** NO LINK TO JUAN CARLOS LERENA HAS BEEN SHOWN. *** *** HIS DEATH IS FOUND: 24 DECEMBER 1901, at seven in the morning, at the house calle Suarez No. 25 in el Paso del Molino, Montevideo. *** Act 216. "De nacionalidad oriental, nacido en Montevideo, de cincuenta y seis [anos], de estado casado, y de profesion HACENDADO" - a landowner, which is the first statement of this family's standing anywhere in the archive. He died of pulmonary tuberculosis, certified by Dr Scremini. *** IT WAS HIDING UNDER A MISSPELLING: *** FamilySearch indexes him as Luis SERENA Lenguas, so every search under LERENA missed him, including a 1,502-row sweep of Montevideo Lerena deaths run the same morning. He was found by searching for his MOTHER. The act also says his father Luis Lerena was already dead, and that his mother Justiniana Lenguas was ALIVE AT 79 and staying in the same house. *** HIS OWN BAPTISM IS NOW READ: born 9 FEBRUARY 1843, baptised 7 January 1846 at the Capilla de la Mauricia, Villa de la Union. *** "Hijo legitimo de Luis Lerena y Justiniana Lenguas, ORIENTALES. Paternos: Francisco y Maria Fernandez. Maternos: Pedro y Carmen Gonzalez." Godparents Juan Lenguas and Maria Fernandez. His death act of 1901 gave his age as 56, implying 1845; the act of his own baptism is the better evidence. *** A THIRD INDEPENDENT RECORD OF THAT DEATH, 14 September 2026: *** the Montevideo cemetery office's own return, "Relacion de los individuos que han fallecido en el mes de Diciembre de 1901", lists him against day 24 between Lucrecia Sosa and Emilia Zanola de Sanchez. *** So he was BURIED AT MONTEVIDEO, and the date now rests on three documents - the civil act, the cemetery roll, and his widow's sworn statement of 1908. *** Found only by searching the COMPOUND surname. *** A CONTRADICTION INSIDE THE REGISTER ITSELF, recorded 14 September 2026 and NOT resolved. *** Luis Eugenio's act says he was born 9 FEBRUARY 1843; his sister Justiniana Mauricia Maxima's act, the entry immediately before his on the same page in the same hand, says she was born 30 JULY 1843. *** That is FIVE AND A HALF MONTHS between two full siblings, and both cannot be right. *** Neither is a machine reading: the transcript of each act has been read verbatim, and both say "del pasado ano cuarenta y tres". *** THE ERROR IS IN THE SOURCE, NOT IN THIS ARCHIVE. *** Every act on that page is a LATER TRANSCRIPT copied out of a legajo by order of Bishop Jacinto Vera - a clerk working from loose papers three years after the events, who had already written "ano cuarenta y tres" twice on the same page. A carried-forward year is the likeliest explanation and it is a guess. Luis Eugenio's death registration of 1901 gives an age and has been read; testing it against 1843 is the next step. *** AND THE CONTRADICTION IS RESOLVED THE SAME AFTERNOON - AGAINST HIS OWN BAPTISM ACT. *** Three facts, two of them already in this archive: (1) his baptism act says he was born 9 February of "el pasado ano cuarenta y tres"; (2) his sister Justiniana Mauricia's act, THE ENTRY IMMEDIATELY ABOVE HIS IN THE SAME HAND, says she was born 30 July 1843 - five and a half months before him, which is impossible; (3) *** his civil death registration of 24 December 1901 gives his age as FIFTY-SIX, which puts his birth at about 1845. *** Two independent constraints point to 1845 and only one points to 1843 - and the one is a clerk copying loose papers three years after the fact, who wrote "ano cuarenta y tres" in the entry above this one and again in the entry below. *** A YEAR CARRIED FORWARD DOWN A COLUMN IS THE ORDINARY WAY THIS ERROR HAPPENS, and it is the only reading under which his sister's date, his own death record and his baptism can all stand. *** *** SO THIS ROW NOW CARRIES 9 FEBRUARY 1845. *** The day and month are secure and are not in question; only the year moved. The act's own words are kept above and in data/1846-la-mauricia-page.tsv, because the source says 1843 and a reader is entitled to see that this archive overruled it and why. *** THIS IS AN INFERENCE, NOT A DOCUMENT *** - an age at death is the weakest date in genealogy and this archive has said so in print; it is load-bearing here only because it agrees with a constraint reached independently of it.

Pedro Lenguas Grandal, is SECONDARY. *** SHE WAS ALIVE ON 24 DECEMBER 1901, AGED 79, and in the house where her son died. *** His death act No. 216 records her "de setenta y nueve anos, de profesion labores, domiciliada accidentalmente en la calle Suarez No. 25" - which puts her birth about 1822 and has her outliving Luis Eugenio. *** AND BY 1908 SHE WAS LIVING IN ARGENTINA, AGED 87. *** Her grandson Jose Julio's birth registration of that year describes her "de ochenta y siete anos, oriental, viuda, labores, RESIDENTE EN LA REPUBLICA ARGENTINA". Lenguas y Dona Carmen Gonzalez." SANCHO y Dona Maria Fernandez". Two acts of 1842 and 1850 now say Sancho against two 1846 entries reading Francisco, and the 1846 pair say of themselves that they are later transcripts from a legajo. *** AND A FOURTH RECORD, THE EARLIEST OF ALL: *** his son's own marriage petition of 3 September 1836, in Luis's hand and over Luis's signature - "hijo legitimo de D. SANCHO LERENA y de Dona Maria Fernandez". Four records now name him, across 1836, 1842 and 1850. *** The doubt raised on 13 September by two 1846 transcripts reading "Francisco" is closed: they are copies, and they are outnumbered by originals. *** *** AND TWO MORE RECORDS, 14 September 2026, neither of them about his son Luis. *** (1) He is named maternal grandfather - "SANCHO LLERENA y MARIA FERNANDEZ" - in the Cordon baptism of 13 December 1831, *** at which the godfather was DON FRUCTUOSO RIVERA, PRESIDENT OF THE REPUBLIC, with his wife Dona Bernardina Fragoso. *** (2) He appears in person as a sworn witness in a marriage investigation at Canelones: "presento por testigo en esta Vicaria a SANCHO LLERENA, a quien se le recivio juramento". Five records now name him. *** AND THEN THE QUESTION REOPENED, the same afternoon. *** The Catedral baptism of Justa Pastora's SECOND child, October 1833 - an ORIGINAL act, not a transcript - names her parents "Maternos: FRANCISCO LERINA y Maria Fernandez". So the Sancho/Francisco alternation is not simply copies against originals, which is what this archive argued an hour earlier and has now withdrawn. *** The one thing constant in every record is the wife, MARIA FERNANDEZ. *** A double forename - Sancho Francisco - would explain it all without anybody being wrong, and is the leading reading. See data/sancho-or-francisco.tsv; his own marriage act would settle it and has never been opened. *** AND THE "AGUILAR" IN HIS NAME HERE IS UNATTESTED. *** None of the eight records now assembled gives him a matronymic; a full-text search for "Llerena y Aguilar" returns thirty hits and every one is QUITO, ECUADOR - a different family. Aguilar comes from the FamilySearch Tree and from nowhere this archive has read. Kept, because the tree may rest on an act nobody here has opened, but marked. *** The forename is contested, the matronymic unsupported, and MARIA FERNANDEZ is the only part of this man's identity every record agrees on. *** *** AND HE IS NOW ATTESTED IN 1804, twenty-seven years earlier than anything this archive held two days ago. *** At Canelones on 15 May 1804 his daughter DOMINGA JOSEFA is baptised "hija legitima de SANCHO LLERENA y de MARIA FERNANDEZ"; in the confirmation list of the same year he stands godfather to "Jose, ESCLAVO DE MANUEL LOPEZ"; and in the marriage-investigation files he gives evidence under oath. *** Father, godfather and sworn witness, in one town, in one decade - and every one of those acts calls him SANCHO. *** The machine transcript renders him SANCIO on the baptism, a sixth spelling for this family. *** AND THEN BACK ANOTHER FIFTEEN YEARS, on 14 September 2026: HE IS IN MONTEVIDEO IN 1789. *** At the Iglesia Matriz on 30 June 1789 the godparents of Juana, daughter of "NICOLAS BENTENO, INDIO NATURAL DE LA CIUDAD DEL TUCUMAN, y de Leonarda Correa de Buenos Ayres", are "SANCHO LLERENA y Juliana Josefa Cornejo". *** He is about twenty-two, unmarried, and in Montevideo two years before the marriage his tree places at Canelones in 1791. *** And it is the second time this archive has found him sponsoring at the margins of colonial society: in 1804 he stood godfather to an ENSLAVED MAN, and here to the daughter of an indigenous man from Tucuman. Twice, fifteen years apart. *** THE TALLY IS ALSO REDONE, AND THE ARCHIVE HAD BEEN COUNTING IT WRONG. *** Fourteen records now name him: ten SANCHO, four FRANCISCO. But THREE OF THE FOUR FRANCISCOS ARE THE SAME PAGE - La Mauricia, 7 January 1846, one clerk writing three acts on one morning out of one legajo. They are one witness, not three. The Sanchos come from nine separate occasions across sixty-one years, in four parishes and two towns, and twice with the man himself present. *** So the evidence is not ten to four. It is nine independent occasions against two, and both of the two describe him at second hand by clerks who never met him. A DOUBLE FORENAME REMAINS THE LEADING READING and explains everything without anyone being wrong - but this archive can no longer call the question evenly balanced. *** *** AND HIS WIFE'S FULL NAME IS NOW ON AN ACT: *** her daughter's marriage of 3 November 1830 calls her "MARIA FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS". This archive carried that matronymic from a PUBLISHED TREE and marked it secondary; the tree was right, about something no index gives. *** Which is a point in favour of that same tree's other unverified claim - that they married at CANELONES on 8 JANUARY 1791. That act has still never been opened. And 'AGUILAR' is STILL unattested across all fourteen records. *** *** AND ON 14 SEPTEMBER 2026, GENEANET SUPPLIES THE ONE THING THIS ROW HAS BEEN CALLING UNATTESTED ALL DAY. *** Two Spanish archive indexes - the Index des mariages catholique de Grenade and Spain, Marriages 1565-1950 - carry a marriage of *** SANCHO LERENA y ARMENTA to ANA MARIA DE AGUILAR, in the DIOCESE OF GRANADA, between 1725 and 1775. *** A son of that couple would be styled *** LERENA y AGUILAR *** - which is exactly the name the trees give this man. So the matronymic is not a tree's invention but a real Spanish naming rule, and it points at a GRANDMOTHER. *** NOT ADOPTED: *** the index has been read and the image has not, the date range is a fifty-year span, and no record yet joins that couple to a son born in 1767. *** But it turns an unattested word into a testable claim in a named diocese, and it is the first thing this archive has ever had that could document this family in SPAIN. *** GRANADA also sits against the trees' CORDOBA - one of them, ckurti, says ZUHEROS, CORDOBA - while the census says only ANDALUZIA, which both satisfy. *** AND FOUR TREES GIVE HIM A DEATH IN 1832, *** where this archive has no death date at all; if true, his son's marriage petition of 1836 names a dead man, which is ordinary. Tree-only, and recorded as a thing to test against Montevideo burials. *** AND ON 14 SEPTEMBER 2026 THE GRANADA ACT ITSELF WAS FOUND - BUT READ THE NEXT SENTENCE BEFORE CREDITING THIS ROW WITH IT. *** The birthplaces below belong to a man in SPAIN in 1754, NOT to the Sancho of this row, and nothing yet joins the two. This archive very nearly wrote the Spanish Cordoba into the Uruguayan Sancho's birthplace field on the strength of it; the field above still says CORDOBA COMES ONLY FROM A TREE, and that is still true of THIS man. *** FamilySearch ark 1:1:C9WG-BGW2 indexes the marriage of *** SANCHO DE LERENA Y ARMENTA to ANA MARIA DE AGUILAR at SANTA ANA, GRANADA on 17 NOVEMBER 1754 *** - the fifty-year span reduced to a day - and it gives the groom's BIRTHPLACE AS CORDOBA and his parents as *** SANCHO DE LERENA Y VELASCO and MARIA ANTONIA DE ARMENTA Y GUEBARA ***, with the bride the daughter of FRANCISCO DE AGUILAR and BEATRIS FRANCO of La Malaha. *** That resolves a tension in the SPANISH record - the Geneanet trees said CORDOBA and the marriage index said GRANADA, and both were right, because he was born at one and married at the other. It does NOT reach across the Atlantic. *** The Uruguayan census's "ANDALUZIA" for the man in this row remains the only birthplace evidence this archive has for HIM, and it is compatible with Cordoba, Granada and much else besides. *** The image is marked IMAGE UNAVAILABLE and has NOT been opened. *** AND THE COMPOUND IS NO LONGER A TREE'S HABIT. *** A Madrid notarial act of 27 March 1790 (ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2C-N7RV) is signed, in the signature position between the witnesses and the notary, *** "JUAN DE LERENA Y AGUILAR" *** - one man, that compound, in the right family and generation, in a Madrid where Sancho de Lerena y Armenta was a vecino from 1766 to 1808. *** BUT NOT ONE RECORD JOINS ANY OF THEM TO THIS MAN. *** A controlled search for children of that couple in Spain returned a genuine null (control: 12 results), and the exact-phrase search for "Sancho de Lerena y Aguilar" returned an UNCONTROLLED "(0)" immediately before FamilySearch blocked the session - *** which is not evidence and is not recorded as a null. *** So "Aguilar" stays exactly where it was: a strong lead with a Spanish family behind it now instead of nothing, and still unattested in all fourteen Uruguayan records. *** The place to look for a 1767 baptism is MADRID, not Granada - the earlier errand said "the same diocese" and was written before the Madrid residence was known. See data/1754-granada-act.tsv. *** *** AND THEN, THE SAME DAY, THE GRANADA READING WAS WITHDRAWN - BY THE VERY TREE THAT SUPPLIES "AGUILAR". *** The jfina Geneanet tree, one of the four this archive cites for the form "Lerena y Aguilar", gives this man's parents as *** FELIX LERENA and ROSALIA AGUILAR ***, born Cordoba about 1767, citing *** APOLANT, "Operativo Patagonia" (Montevideo 1970), FICHA 355 ***. *** So AGUILAR is his MOTHER'S SURNAME - ordinary Spanish naming - and not a grandmother from Granada. *** The morning's inference, that the compound must descend from the 1754 Granada couple, was a naming rule applied to a name whose actual owner is recorded elsewhere; and the controlled null against that couple is explained rather than puzzling. *** The Spanish search that matters now is FELIX LERENA and ROSALIA AGUILAR at CORDOBA, which is not the search that was run. *** AND THE MARRIAGE DATE FINALLY HAS A REAL SOURCE WHILE THE PLACE LOSES ITS ONE: *** 8 January 1791 comes from Apolant ficha 355, a named published work; *** "Canelones" appears nowhere in it *** - the note's "Concejo de Morcin, Asturias" is the BRIDE'S birthplace, she being JOSEFA FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS b.1778 at Morcin, an ASTURIAN of the Operativo Patagonia convoy, daughter of RODRIGO FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS and ROSA FERNANDEZ. *** Canelones remains the strong inference because the 1812 padron lists all six children as "naturales del Canelon", the eldest 21. *** THE 1812 PADRON ALSO HOLDS WHAT THIS ROW DID NOT: *** calle San Juan No 60, Sancho "andaluz" 45, Maria Fernandez 36, children Juan Agustin 21, Pedro Antonio 19, Agustina 17, Fidel 12, Justa 10 and DOMINGA 7 - all "naturales del Canelon" - *** his father-in-law RODRIGO FERNANDEZ, 63, asturiano, living in the house, and FOUR ENSLAVED PEOPLE *** (AGN, Fondo ex AGA, L 251). See data/apolant-ficha-355.tsv. *** AND ON 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 HIS PARENTS ARRIVED ON AN ACT, WHICH CLOSES THE LAST WEAK JOINT IN THIS ROW. *** At the Iglesia Matriz of Montevideo on 10 February 1811, at the baptism of his son LUIS ESCOLASTICO, the act names him *** "Don SANCHO LLERENA natural de ANDALUCIA" *** and his parents *** "Abuelos paternos FELIZ GERENA y ROSALIA AGUILAR" *** - GERENA being the machine's G-for-L, a seventh variant for this family. *** Until that morning FELIX LERENA and ROSALIA AGUILAR rested on ONE un-consulted journal article reported at second hand through one tree, and this row said so. *** *** They are now on a parish act written while he was alive and standing at his own son's font. *** *** ANDALUCIA IS ALSO NOW ON AN ACT *** and no longer only on the 1726-1858 census. *** CORDOBA IS STILL ON NO ACT *** and remains what the trees say, citing Apolant ficha 355. *** AND THE TALLY OF HIS SPONSORSHIPS IS WRONG IN THIS ROW AND IS CORRECTED, 15 September 2026. *** It says he stood godfather at the margins of colonial society "twice, fifteen years apart" - the indigenous man's daughter in 1789 and an enslaved man in 1804. *** It is at least FOUR times, and three of them on one day. *** Three further pages of the 1804 Canelones confirmations name him as padrino, including "Joseph Jimenez ESCLAVO DE DON LUIS JIMENEZ. P. Sancho Llerena" - a different enslaved man with a different owner from the Jose, esclavo de Manuel Lopez, already recorded here. *** The pattern is now too consistent to read as chance. *** *** A NEW CHILD IS ALSO ADDED: JUSTA PASTORA, baptised at Canelones on 9 August 1800, born three days earlier *** - this archive had her only from her 1830 marriage and from the padron's rough age of 10. *** That act transcribes the mother as 'MARIA RODRIGO', which is not her name in any of the other fourteen records. *** The most economical reading is that a clerk wrote her father's forename - RODRIGO Fernandez - and that only became visible once the 1811 act named him. *** The image has not been opened and the discrepancy is left standing. *** *** AND ON 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 THREE MORE ACTS ARRIVED, BECAUSE THE NAME WAS FINALLY SEARCHED WITH ONE L. *** Every full-text sweep here had been run on SANCHO LLERENA. "Sancho LERENA" returns three Canelones baptisms that were not among them. *** HIS RANK: the 1793 act calls him "el SOLDADO DRAGON Sancho Lerena" - a dragoon, where the census says only soldado. *** *** HIS REGIMENT, BY IMPLICATION: that act was performed by "el Capellan del REGIMIENTO DE INFANTERIA DE BUENOS AYRES Don Bartolome Munoz" *** - the same regiment whose Libros Castrenses of 1781-1814 are filmed as DGS 7713373. *** His 1791 marriage may well be in those military books, and the reason to look is now documented rather than hopeful. *** *** HIS WIFE IS CALLED TERESA: *** at a Canelones baptism of 27 October 1805 the godparents are "SANCHO LERENA y MARIA TERESA FERNANDEZ de este Pueblo" - the trees give her as Maria Josefa (TERESA) Fernandez Tresguerras and this archive had marked those forenames tree-only. *** AND THE SPONSORSHIP COUNT RISES AGAIN, to five. ***

name: Jose Julio LERENA Juanico
occupation: JUEZ DE PAZ y Oficial del Estado Civil, 1a Seccion de Montevideo (strong, not proved)
source: Montevideo civil birth registration No. 283 of 1908 - IMAGE READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-W97S-F; and thirty-five Montevideo civil marriage acts of 1902-1914 signed "Julio Lerena Juanico, Juez de Paz" - one read in full, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-2SKF-F
note: *** A SIXTH CHILD of Luis Eugenio Lerena Lenguas and Julia Juanico, found 13 September 2026. *** Born 15 March 1879 at Montevideo and not registered until 14 September 1908, when he was 29 - a late registration of the kind a man makes to produce proof of birth for his own wedding, and he does appear on a Montevideo marriage index card for 1908. *** THE IMAGE IS OPENED. *** Born at the house calle YI No. 303, and registered in 1908 by HIS OWN MOTHER - Dona Julia Juanico, 64, a widow of calle Buenos Aires 102. The act independently confirms Luis Eugenio's death, "fallecido en esta Ciudad el veinte y cuatro de Diciembre de mil novecientos uno", from a different document written seven years after it. *** AND IT PLACES JUSTINIANA LENGUAS, AT EIGHTY-SEVEN, RESIDENT IN THE ARGENTINE REPUBLIC. *** *** AND HE WAS ALMOST CERTAINLY A JUDGE. *** Thirty-five Montevideo civil marriage acts of 1902-1914 open "Por ante mi JULIO LERENA JUANICO, JUEZ DE PAZ y OFICIAL DEL ESTADO CIVIL de la Primera Seccion del Departamento de Montevideo". The compound surname is this family's and no other here; he is the only JULIO among the seven children; and he would be thirty in 1909. *** STRONG BUT NOT PROVED - no act read so far gives the judge's own parents. *** And it explains the oddest thing in his record: a man appointed Oficial del Estado Civil needs proof of his own birth rather more than a bridegroom does, which is why his widowed mother swore it before a Juzgado de Paz in September 1908.

note: *** A SEVENTH CHILD, and the best-documented of them all. *** Baptised 6 July 1886 at 21 months: "hijo legitimo de Don Luis Lerena Lenguas y de Dona Julia Juanico, orientales". name: Alejandro LERENA TRAIBEL (formerly recorded as LERENA LENGUAS)
source: La Mauricia, Villa de la Union, Montevideo, baptised 7 Jan 1846 - IMAGE READ and FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-ZS62-J
note: *** CORRECTED 14 SEPTEMBER 2026, AND THE CORRECTION MOVES HIM BETWEEN BRANCHES. *** This archive recorded him on 13 September as "A SIXTH CHILD of Luis Lerena and Justiniana Lenguas", born 29 May 1845. *** BOTH HALVES WERE WRONG. *** The act reads: "bautizo solemnemente a ALEJANDRO, que nacio el veinte y nueve de Mayo del pasado ano CUARENTA Y TRES, hijo legitimo de AVELINO SERENA y AMBROSIA TRAIBEL. Paternos FRANCISCO y MARIA FERNANDEZ. Maternos JUAN e ISABEL CENTENO. Padrinos LUIS [L]ERENA y JUSTINIANA LENGUAS." *** He is a son of AVELINO, not of Luis - and Luis and Justiniana are his GODPARENTS, which is how the archive came to read them as his parents. *** The two brothers brought their children to the same font on the same morning and stood for each other's. *** So he is the ELDEST KNOWN CHILD OF AVELINO LERENA AND AMBROSIA TRAIBEL *** - eight years before Josefa, fifteen before Alfredo - and he pushes their marriage back before May 1843. *** AND HE IS A FOURTH ALEJANDRO. *** See data/the-three-alejandros.tsv: the enrolment cards of Cajon 985 name an ALEJANDRO MAXIMO LERENA, born Uruguay 1839, whose parents no record here names. Four years apart from this man. NOTHING POSITIVE LINKS THEM and they stay separate rows, but the candidate pool has changed and the table needs re-reading.

name: General Don Pedro LENGUAS
source: Named as maternal grandfather in the 1846 baptisms at La Mauricia - IMAGE READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-ZS62-J
note: *** Father of JUSTINIANA and of SIXTA Lenguas, and called "el GENERAL" in his granddaughter's baptism act. *** Through Justiniana he is great-grandfather to Gilberto Lerena's children; through Sixta he is father-in-law to Dr Candido Juanico. He also stood godfather at his granddaughter's christening. *** HIS OWN PARENTS ARE NOW NAMED: D. ANTONIO LENGUAS and Dona JUANA GRANDAL *** - from his daughter Sixta's death act of 1884, image read. That is a generation this archive had never reached. *** THE RANK IS CONFIRMED IN A SECOND ACT, four years earlier: *** his daughter's marriage of 3 March 1842 calls her "hija legitima del Sr. GRAL. Lenguas y Dona Carmen Gonzalez". *** AND IT EXPLAINS A FAMILYSEARCH GHOST: *** the index of that act renders "Gral. D. Pedro" as a forename - "Geraldo Dios Lenguas" - which is how a military rank turns into a christian name and a searchable person who never existed.

name: Dona Maria FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS (wife of Sancho)
source: Named as paternal grandmother in the 1850 act, and as godmother in 1846 - IMAGE READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-ZSZQ-J; and her daughter Justa Pastora's marriage act, Cordon, 3 Nov 1830 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-B3WZ-8; Montevideo, Iglesia Matriz, baptism of Luis Escolastico, 10 Feb 1811 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-X7F6-M
note: Wife of Sancho Llerena and mother of Don Luis Lerena - which is where the "y Fernandez" in his name comes from. She stood godmother at her grandson Luis Eugenio's baptism in 1846. *** HER FULL NAME IS ON AN ACT, 14 September 2026 - and it vindicates a tree. *** Her daughter's marriage of 3 November 1830 names the bride "hija legitima de Sancho Llerena y de MARIA FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS". This archive has carried "Maria Josefa Fernandez Tresguerras" since its first week FROM A PUBLISHED TREE, marked secondary, with the matronymic unverified. *** The tree was right, and right about something no index anywhere gives. *** Which raises the standing of that same tree's other unopened claim - that she married Sancho at CANELONES on 8 JANUARY 1791. *** SHE IS ALSO THE ONE FIXED POINT IN HER HUSBAND'S IDENTITY: *** across fourteen records his forename alternates between Sancho and Francisco, and every single one of them names HER. *** The Geneanet trees give her more fully as MARIA JOSEFA FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS, and two of them add TERESA. *** Today's marriage act says only "Maria Fernandez Tresguerras" - but since that act has just vindicated the trees on TRESGUERRAS itself, the extra forenames are worth more than they were yesterday. Still tree-only, and not adopted. *** HER BIRTHPLACE AND HER PARENTS ARE NOW ON AN ACT, 15 September 2026. *** The 1811 baptism of her son Luis calls her *** "Dona MARIA FERNANDEZ natural de ASTURIAS" *** and names *** "abuelos maternos RODRIGO FERNANDEZ y ROSA FERNANDEZ" *** *** ASTURIAS confirms the Operativo Patagonia reading from a Uruguayan document *** - her family were of the 1778-1781 convoy, 41 Asturian founder families of which seven came from MORCIN, the concejo the trees give as her birthplace. *** And RODRIGO FERNANDEZ is the same man the 1812 padron records living in Sancho's household, aged 63, "asturiano" *** - so the household, the act and the trees agree on him from three directions.

name: Dona Carolina ORIBE (1st wife of Don Luis Lerena)
source: Marriage petition of 3 September 1836, Arquidiocesis de Montevideo - IMAGE READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-J331-G; and named as his deceased first wife in the act of 3 March 1842; and named with her husband as godmother in the Catedral baptism of 4 July 1837 - ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-YSKH-H
note: *** HER SURNAME IS ORIBE, AND THIS ARCHIVE RECORDED IT WRONG TWICE. *** She was written here as Carolina OLIVA, from the 1836 marriage petition and from FamilySearch's index of it - which says Oliva, and which is where the reading came from. The Catedral baptism of 4 July 1837, a different book in a different hand, names her "Dna CAROLINA ORIBE" standing godmother with her husband to his brother's child. The 1836 petition was then re-opened and magnified: it reads ORIBE there too, with a clear b. *** And the published genealogy this archive has always tiered as SECONDARY said all along that Don Luis married firstly a daughter of an ORIBE. It was right. *** She married Luis Lerena at Montevideo in September 1836, was ALIVE IN JULY 1837, and was dead by March 1842 when he remarried "en segundas nupcias". *** ORIBE is one of the great Uruguayan names - Manuel Oribe was President 1835-1838 and founder of the Blancos - but NOTHING READ HERE MAKES HER HIS KIN. *** Oribe is a surname, not a proof, and no record yet names her parents. *** PLACE FIELD CORRECTED 14 September 2026. *** This row's 'where found' held a CITATION - an empty placeholder - where the atlas expects a PLACE, so this person was missing from the map and appeared on it as a phantom location instead. The citation is kept here; the field now holds a real place.

name: Justa Pastora LERENA (daughter of Sancho)
source: Nuestra Senora del Carmen la Mayor, Cordon, Montevideo, baptism of 13 Dec 1831 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-CS9Z-2; and her own MARRIAGE, Nuestra Senora del Carmen La Mayor, Cordon, Montevideo, 3 Nov 1830 - index read, ark 1:1:X9PT-MQTQ, FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-B3WZ-8
note: *** A DAUGHTER OF SANCHO LLERENA AND MARIA FERNANDEZ, and so a SISTER OF DON LUIS LERENA - found 14 September 2026 and previously unknown to this archive. *** Named in the Cordon baptism of her son on 13 December 1831 as "Justa Pastora Lerena, natural de CANELONES", wife of Manuel Zeferino Barros of Pernambuco. *** Her son's godparents were the PRESIDENT OF THE REPUBLIC and his wife. *** *** A SECOND CHILD, October 1833, at the Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion *** - and its act names her parents FRANCISCO LERINA and Maria Fernandez, where her first child's act of 1831 said SANCHO LLERENA. She is the person through whom the alternation became visible. Her second child's godparents were ABELINO and DOMINGA LERENA. *** HER MARRIAGE IS NOW DATED: 3 NOVEMBER 1830, at the Cordon *** - to MANUEL BARROS, with her parents given as Sancho Llerena and Maria Fernandez and her birthplace as Canelones. *** Which puts THIRTEEN MONTHS between the wedding and the font at which FRUCTUOSO RIVERA stood godfather to her first child, *** in the same parish, on 13 December 1831. The index has been read and the image has not, so the date is SECONDARY; her parentage is PRIMARY from the 1831 act. *** AND THE ACT ITSELF IS NOW READ, not merely its index. *** "En tres de Noviembre de mil ochocientos treinta, precedidas informacion de libertad de MANUEL ZEFERINO BARROS natural de PERNAMBUCO, hijo legitimo de Jose [P]olanda de Barros y de Ana Maria Cabalgante, sobre el Matrimonio que libremente quiere contraer con JUSTA PASTORA LLERENA, NATURAL DE CANELONES, RESIDENTE EN EL CORDON, hija legitima de SANCHO LLERENA y de MARIA FERNANDEZ TRESGUERRAS." *** THREE GAINS IN ONE SENTENCE: *** she was already living at the Cordon before she married there; her mother's matronymic TRESGUERRAS is on a document for the first time; and the date is no longer index-level. The parish is DAMASO ANTONIO LARRANAGA'S - he is marrying another couple on the same page.

name: Abelino LERENA (godfather, 1833)
source: Named as godparent at the Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, Montevideo, baptism of Oct 1833 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-YSKW-T
note: *** A LERENA MAN OF SANCHO'S OWN GENERATION OR THE NEXT, found 14 September 2026. *** He stood godfather with Dominga Lerena at the Catedral in October 1833 to a child of Justa Pastora Lerena - so almost certainly her brother or cousin. The transcript renders him "Abelino Serena", one more instance of the S-for-L this archive has met before. *** AVELINO is also the forename attached to the LERENA TRAIBEL branch elsewhere in this archive, which is worth testing rather than assuming. *** *** THE AGE NOW FITS, WHICH IS NOT THE SAME AS PROOF. *** Avelino Lerena Fernandez, Sancho's son, is now dated to a birth of 1815 - so he was EIGHTEEN in October 1833. Young for a godfather and entirely possible, and he would have been standing for his own sister's child. *** STILL KEPT AS A SEPARATE ROW *** until a record joins them, for the reason the two Arturos exist in this archive.

name: Dominga Josefa LLERENA Fernandez (b.1804)
source: Catedral Nuestra Senora de Guadalupe, Canelones, baptism of 15 May 1804 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2Z-W9V2-Y; and named as godmother at the Catedral de Montevideo, Oct 1833; and the Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, Montevideo, baptism of her daughter Lucinda Gregoria, 12 May 1827 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-YSFQ-2; and the Catedral baptism of her son Domingo, 25 Oct 1840 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-YSFY-L
note: *** A DAUGHTER OF SANCHO LLERENA AND MARIA FERNANDEZ, and now dated: born 13 May 1804 at Canelones, baptised two days later. *** "Una parvula de dos dias nacida, a la cual puso por nombre Dominga Josefa, hija legitima de Sancho Llerena y de Maria Fernandez; fueron los padrinos Joseph Ponteceli y Agueda Rivero, TODOS VECINOS DE LA MISMA VILLA." *** She is the DOMINGA LERENA who stood godmother at the Catedral de Montevideo in October 1833 to her sister Justa Pastora's child *** - aged twenty-nine. The archive guessed "almost certainly her sister or cousin"; she is the sister. A SISTER OF DON LUIS LERENA. *** A CAUTION ADDED 14 September 2026, AND NOT RESOLVED. *** Two indexed records name a Dominga, daughter of Sancho and Maria Fernandez, with DIFFERENT HUSBANDS: one "Dominga Lorena" married to ANTONIO RODRIGUEZ with a son Domingo (ark 1:1:6D7C-5X1Y), and one "Dominga Llarena" married to ANTONIO RUIZ DE CARVALLO with a daughter Lucinda Gregoria (ark 1:1:6DF7-HZPR). The image arks are adjacent, so the two acts are near neighbours in one register. That is either ONE WOMAN WHO MARRIED TWICE, ONE MAN WHOSE NAME IS WRITTEN TWO WAYS, or TWO SISTERS OF THE SAME FORENAME - and this archive has been caught by exactly that shape twice, with the two Arturos and the three Josefas. Both husbands being ANTONIO is suggestive and is not proof. *** NEITHER IMAGE OPENED; NOTHING MERGED INTO THIS ROW. *** See data/sancho-children-complete.tsv. Note also that a DONA DOMINGA CARVALLO stood godmother at a Lerena font in 1850, which makes the CARVALLO husband worth reading rather than assuming. *** THE CAUTION ABOVE IS NOW HALF ANSWERED - ON AN ACT, the same afternoon it was written. *** The Catedral baptism of 12 May 1827 reads: "Lucinda Gregoria del Corazon de Jesus, que nacio en veinte y cuatro de Abril ultimo, hija legitima del CAPITAN DON ANTONIO RUIZ DE CARVALLO, y de DONA DOMINGA LLERENA DE CARVALLO. Nieta Paterna del MAYOR DON JOAQUIN RUIZ DE CARVALLO y de la finada Dona Juana Suarez; MATERNA DE SANCHO LLERENA Y DE DONA MARIA FERNANDEZ." *** So Sancho's daughter Dominga married a CAPTAIN, son of a MAJOR - and the godfather was EXCELENTISIMO SENOR GENERAL DON FRANCISCO DE PAULA MAGGESI. *** A second general at a Lerena font. *** AND IT IDENTIFIES A WOMAN THIS ARCHIVE COULD NOT PLACE: *** the "DONA DOMINGA CARVALLO" who stood godmother at Alberto Octavio Lerena's baptism in 1850 is almost certainly this woman - Dominga Llerena de Carvallo, standing for her brother's son. Not merged, because the 1850 act gives her only as Carvallo; but the two rows should be read together. *** THE OTHER DOMINGA RECORD - the one naming a husband ANTONIO RODRIGUEZ and a son DOMINGO - IS STILL UNRESOLVED *** and its image is still unopened. One woman twice married, or a sister of the same name. *** AND THEN FULLY RESOLVED, an hour later, BY OPENING THE SECOND IMAGE. *** The Catedral act of 25 October 1840 reads: "bautice solemnemente a DOMINGO que nacio el cuatro de Agosto del presente ano, hijo legitimo de D. ANTONIO RODRIGUEZ DE CARBALLO, natural de la PROVINCIA DEL RIO GRANDE, y de Dona DOMINGA LERENA, natural del Estado Oriental. Nieto paterno de D. JOAQUIN RODRIGUEZ y de Dona JUANA DEL ESPIRITU SANTO, ambos naturales de la COLONIA DEL SACRAMENTO, y por parte materna de D. SANCHO LERENA y de Dona MARIA FERNANDEZ." *** THE TWO HUSBANDS ARE ONE MAN. *** "Antonio Rodriguez" and "Antonio Ruiz de Carvallo" are the same Antonio DE CARVALLO, whose first surname the registers write RUIZ in 1827 and RODRIGUEZ in 1840, and whose father is JOAQUIN in both. *** THERE IS ONE DOMINGA, AND SHE IS THIS ONE. *** Her known children are LUCINDA GREGORIA (b. 24 April 1827) and DOMINGO (b. 4 August 1840) - thirteen years apart, so there are almost certainly others between them. *** TWO DISCREPANCIES RECORDED RATHER THAN SMOOTHED: *** 1827 makes Antonio a CAPITAN and his father a MAYOR and names the mother DONA JUANA SUAREZ, "la finada"; 1840 gives no ranks, makes Antonio a native of RIO GRANDE in Brazil with parents from the COLONIA DEL SACRAMENTO, and names the mother DONA JUANA DEL ESPIRITU SANTO. A devotional epithet and a surname can belong to one woman - Juana del Espiritu Santo Suarez - and that is a reading, not a finding.

source: Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion, Montevideo, baptism of 4 July 1837 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-YSKH-H; Canelones baptism, 1 Aug 1793 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-CS2Z-WH52
note: *** ANOTHER SON OF SANCHO LLERENA AND MARIA FERNANDEZ, and so another BROTHER OF DON LUIS - found 14 September 2026. *** "D. PEDRO ANTONIO LERENA natural de esta", with "Abuelos Paternos: D. Sancho y Dna Maria Fernandez" named at his daughter's baptism on 4 July 1837. He married DONA VICENTA VEGA of Cerro Largo. His brother Luis and Luis's wife Carolina Oribe stood godparents to the child. *** HIS BAPTISM ACT IS FOUND, 15 September 2026, and it carries two things about his FATHER that nothing else did. *** Canelones, 1 August 1793: "El Capellan del REGIMIENTO DE INFANTERIA DE BUENOS AYRES Don Bartolome Munoz; bautizo puso oleo y crisma a PEDRO ANTONIO DE LA SSMA TRINIDAD que nacio ayer, hijo legitimo del SOLDADO DRAGON SANCHO LERENA, y de Maria Fernandez, fueron Padrinos Don Antonio Aleman, y su mujer Dona Gregoria Ribero." *** Born 31 July 1793 - this archive had only the year, from a tree, and an age of 19 in the 1812 padron. *** *** His full baptismal name is PEDRO ANTONIO DE LA SANTISIMA TRINIDAD. *** *** His father is called SOLDADO DRAGON - a dragoon - where every other record says only soldado. *** *** AND THE PRIEST IS THE CHAPLAIN OF THE REGIMIENTO DE INFANTERIA DE BUENOS AIRES *** - the exact unit whose Libros Castrenses, 1781-1814, are filmed as FamilySearch DGS 7713373. *** That makes the military registers the first place to look for Sancho's 1791 marriage rather than a hopeful one, because that regiment's chaplain was demonstrably serving this family at Canelones two years after it. ***

name: Josefa in Gilberto's 1895 household (b. c.1852)
source: Argentina, National Census 1895, Ciudad de la Capital, Seccion 21, Manzana 15 - IMAGE READ; ark 3:1:S3HT-DZTW-9S9; and named as godmother at the Catedral de Montevideo, 10 Sep 1885, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-BQZD-W
note: *** ALMOST CERTAINLY THE JOSEFA LERENA WHO STOOD GODMOTHER TO GILBERTO'S SON RAUL at the Catedral de Montevideo on 10 September 1885 *** - a woman this archive met and could not place. The 1895 census finds her in Gilberto's own Buenos Aires household: "Lerena de L. Josefa, m, 43, VIUDA, R. Oriental". Born about 1852, so of his generation. *** THE FORM OF HER NAME IS 'LERENA DE L.' *** On the two lines above her the enumerator writes married women as [maiden surname] de L. - Lenguas de Lerena, Salvanach de Lerena. If he is consistent, SHE WAS BORN A LERENA AND MARRIED A LERENA. *** That is the exact pattern behind this archive's standing question - whether Maria Lerena, named on Pablo Armando's enrolment card, was a Lerena by birth. *** Stated as a reading of an abbreviation in an enumerator's hand, not as a fact: her own marriage record would settle it and has not been looked for. *** CORRECTED WITHIN THE HOUR: THE 'DE LERENA' READING IS WITHDRAWN AS EVIDENCE. *** Uruguayan civil registration carries a JOSEFA LERENA married to FERNANDO MORATORIO, and FamilySearch's tree attaches her to Josefa Lerena Traibel 1851-1947 - the same candidate. If that is this woman, "de L." is the enumerator's shorthand for the LERENA HOUSEHOLD rather than her husband's surname, and this entry says nothing about a Lerena-Lerena marriage. The letter was read right; the inference was not. See data/josefa-lerena-candidates.tsv. *** AND THE WITHDRAWAL IS NOW ON A DOCUMENT RATHER THAN A TREE. *** The 1880 baptisms of Josefa Lerena's daughters name her husband Fernando Moratorio and her parents Avelino and Ambrosia Traibel. If this census woman is that Josefa - she is 43 here against a birth of 1851, and a VIUDA where a later record calls Fernando Moratorio "fallecido" - then "de L." is the enumerator's shorthand for the LERENA HOUSEHOLD and nothing more.

name: Josefa LERENA TRAIBEL (1851-1947)
source: Montevideo civil death registration No. 10, 3 April 1947 - index read; ark 1:1:617P-WJY6, image 3:1:3Q9M-CS2C-DPLX; and the baptisms of her two daughters, Union, Montevideo, 8 Mar 1880 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-ZS46-J
note: *** DAUGHTER OF AVELINO LERENA AND AMBROSIA TRAIBEL - which places the LERENA TRAIBEL branch this archive has named since its first week. *** Died 2 April 1947 at Montevideo, aged NINETY-SIX. *** A STRONG CANDIDATE for the Josefa Lerena who stood godmother at the Catedral in 1885 and for the "Lerena de L. Josefa, 43, viuda" in Gilberto's 1895 Buenos Aires household - the ages agree within a year. DELIBERATELY NOT MERGED WITH THEM: *** this archive conflated two Arturo Lerenas in the same week and had to retract a branch within the hour. See data/josefa-lerena-candidates.tsv for what fits and what is untested. *** AND SHE MARRIED A MORATORIO, NOT A LERENA - NOW ON A PARISH ACT. *** Uruguayan civil registration names a Josefa Lerena as mother of Josefa, Eduardo and Maria MORATORIO LERENA, "Spouses: Fernando Moratorio", and the FamilySearch tree attaches that woman to this one. The marriage records are index-level and real; the link between the two women is a TREE ATTACHMENT and therefore SECONDARY. *** THE TREE ATTACHMENT IS NO LONGER NEEDED: *** the baptisms of her daughters MARIA CARLOTA and MARIA DE LAS MERCEDES MORATORIO LERENA at Union, Montevideo on 8 March 1880 name the parents "Fernando Moratorio y Josefa Lerena" and the maternal grandparents "AVELINO y AMBROSIA TRAIBEL". So the Moratorio wife and the daughter of Avelino are one woman, on a document.

name: Avelino LERENA Fernandez (son of Sancho)
source: Named as father in the Montevideo death registration of Josefa Lerena Traibel, 3 April 1947 - ark 1:1:617P-WJY6; and as maternal grandfather in two Union baptisms of 8 Mar 1880 - ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-ZS46-J; and as father of the groom in the Catedral marriage of 3 Feb 1892 - ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-R32C-K; and TWO baptisms of his children, San Francisco de Asis, 12 Mar 1858, naming his parents - San Francisco de Asis, Montevideo, baptisms of 12 Mar 1858 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ; ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-NRM4; and his own MONTEVIDEO CIVIL DEATH REGISTRATION of 23 Aug 1890 - index read, ark 1:1:62J2-4CNQ, image 3:1:3Q9M-CS2W-K796-D NOT YET OPENED; and the baptism of his son ALEJANDRO at La Mauricia, Villa de la Union, 7 Jan 1846 - FULL-TEXT TRANSCRIPT READ, ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9BW-ZS62-J
note: *** THE HEAD OF THE LERENA TRAIBEL BRANCH, named at last on 14 September 2026. *** Husband of AMBROSIA TRAIBEL and father of Josefa Lerena Traibel, born 1851. This archive has referred to the Lerena Traibel since its first week without ever placing Avelino. *** HE IS SANCHO'S SON - SETTLED 14 September 2026 ON A PARISH ACT. *** An Avelino Lerena stood godfather at the Catedral de Montevideo in 1833 to a child of Justa Pastora Lerena, Sancho's daughter, which is suggestive and no more. No record found here names Avelino's own parents. *** AND HE IS NAMED IN A PARISH ACT, not only in a death index: *** the baptisms of his granddaughters at Union on 8 March 1880 give "abuelos maternos AVELINO y AMBROSIA TRAIBEL". *** A SECOND CHILD FOUND, 14 September 2026: ALFREDO, born about 1857, married at the Catedral Basilica on 3 February 1892 *** - "hijo legitimo de Don AVELINO LORENA y Dona Ambrosia Traibel". So Avelino and Ambrosia had at least JOSEFA (1851) and ALFREDO (c.1857), and probably MERCEDES, who stood godmother in 1880. *** TWO BAPTISMS OF 12 MARCH 1858 AT SAN FRANCISCO DE ASIS name the paternal grandparents of his children as SANCHO LERENA and MARIA FERNANDEZ - twice, on one page. *** So the whole LERENA TRAIBEL line descends from Sancho, and several of its members were already floating unattached in this register: Mercedes Micaela and Clorinda in the dispensation table, and JUAN ARTURO - the man this archive conflated with another Arturo in its first week and had to retract. *** And the godparents at those two fonts were LAVALLEJA - Justiniano, Constantino and Ana. *** *** AND HE NOW HAS DATES, 14 September 2026: BORN 1815, DIED 22 AUGUST 1890 at Montevideo, registered the next day. *** The registration names his parents Sancho and Maria Fernandez - an INDEPENDENT attestation of the parentage the 1858 baptisms settled, and the first record in this archive to say when Avelino lived. *** IT ALSO EXPLAINS SOMETHING THE ARCHIVE HAD ONLY NOTED AS ODD. *** At his son Alfredo's wedding in February 1892 the witness was AMBROSIA TRAIBEL, the mother, where a father would be expected. Avelino had been dead sixteen months. Three records - the 1858 fonts, this registration, and the 1892 marriage - now lock together in one order. The registration spells him LEVENA, an eighth spelling. The image has not been opened, so the dates are SECONDARY; the parentage is PRIMARY from 1858. *** AND AN ELDEST CHILD, found 14 September 2026 - by correcting one of this archive's own rows. *** ALEJANDRO, born 29 May 1843, baptised at La Mauricia on 7 January 1846, "hijo legitimo de Avelino Serena y Ambrosia Traibel" - a boy this archive had wrongly recorded as a sixth child of his brother Luis. So Avelino and Ambrosia were married before May 1843, and their known children run ALEJANDRO (1843), JOSEFA (1851), ALFREDO JUSTINIANO and ANA ROSARIO (1858), probably MERCEDES. *** And the act shows the two brothers standing as godparents for each other's children at the same font on the same morning *** - Luis and Justiniana for Alejandro, while Luis's own two were christened in the entries just above.

name: Ambrosia TRAIBEL
source: Named as mother in the Montevideo death registration of Josefa Lerena Traibel, 3 April 1947 - ark 1:1:617P-WJY6; and as a witness at her son Alfredo's marriage, 3 Feb 1892 - ark 3:1:3Q9M-C9B7-R32C-K
note: Wife of Avelino Lerena and mother of Josefa Lerena Traibel (1851-1947). She is the TRAIBEL of the Lerena Traibel branch. *** SHE WAS ALIVE IN FEBRUARY 1892 AND STOOD WITNESS AT HER SON'S WEDDING: *** "fueron testigos Don Carlos Navia y Dona AMBROSIA TRAIBEL" - which is unusual enough to be worth noting; a mother as formal witness rather than a male relative. *** HER OWN PARENTS ARE NAMED: JUAN TRAIBEL and YSABEL CENTENO *** - from the two baptisms of 12 March 1858. This archive argued that "Juan Agustin cannot be Sancho's son, who would be a child in 1812" and talked itself out of the reading. *** He was twenty-one, and his sister Agustina was seventeen. *** The two names at that font are his and hers, and the child baptised was very likely their first cousin. *** So SERENA and PERENA are the machine's S-for-L again - the sixth time on this family. *** The tree gives his birth as 1792; the padron implies 1791.
